sub_criteria.name: extraction accuracy
sub_criteria.text: Measures LLM claim-extraction accuracy from full papers or abstracts against expert/human annotation, ideally broken down by paper section, claim type, or model.

sub_criteria.name: evidence-link errors
sub_criteria.text: Characterizes how claim-to-evidence links (passage, table, or citation) fail: fabricated support, wrong-direction reads of contradicting evidence, or over-generalisation past the paper's conditions.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Describes how a claim-evidence or citation-grounding benchmark (e.g. SciFact, CiteME, or similar) was built, and what its reported numbers can or cannot legitimately support.

sub_criteria.name: abstention and calibration
sub_criteria.text: Tests whether abstention or calibrated uncertainty improves the trustworthiness of extracted claims, and reports the coverage cost of doing so.

sub_criteria.name: cross-model or cross-domain generalisation
sub_criteria.text: Reports whether extraction or grounding results replicate across different models, domains, or paper types, or whether they are inflated by benchmark artifacts.

items.abstract_600: Claim verification splits between end-to-end classifiers that are accurate but yields no inspectable traces, and decomposition-based methods produce inspectable traces but lag performance on benchmark datasets. We propose DecomposeRL an accurate claim-verifier that produce inspectable traces. DecomposeRL frames decomposition as an RL policy trained with GRPO and a multi-faceted reward ensemble, enabling both fully supervised and semi-supervised learning from unlabeled claims. items.title: A Multi-Stage Hallucination Reduction Framework for Large Language Models using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and NLI-based Verification
items.abstract_600: Strong generative abilities are displayed by Large Language Models (LLMs), but they often generate hallucinations—confident but factually incorrect statements. The safe use of LLMs in academic, legal, medical, and business applications that demand factual reliability is complicated by these hallucinations. This work describes a multi-phase framework for reducing hallucinations that combines a verification module based on Natural Language Inference (NLI) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). items.title: Parametric Retrieval Augmented Generation
items.abstract_600: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising solution to enhance the reliability of large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge. Existing RAG methods share a common strategy for knowledge injection: they place the retrieved documents into the input context of the LLM, which we refer to as the in-context knowledge injection method. items.abstract_600: Retrieval-augmented generation systems for legal question answering typically retrieve passages based on semantic similarity and provide them to a language model, which then generates cited answers. items.title: A Hybrid Approach to Semi-automated Rust Verification
items.abstract_600: We propose a hybrid approach to end-to-end Rust verification where the proof effort is split into powerful automated verification of safe Rust and targeted semi-automated verification of unsafe Rust. items.title: SciClaimEval: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers
items.abstract_600: We present SciClaimEval, a new scientific dataset for the claim verification task. Unlike existing resources, SciClaimEval features authentic claims, including refuted ones, directly extracted from published papers. To create refuted claims, we introduce a novel approach that modifies the supporting evidence (figures and tables), rather than altering the claims or relying on large language models (LLMs) to fabricate contradictions. items.abstract_600: Evidence-based science depends on the iterative integration of experimentation, a process traditionally driven by slow and error-prone human effort. items.abstract_600: Quotations are crucial to science but have been shown to be often inaccurate. Quotation errors, that is, a reference not supporting the authors’ claim, may still be a significant issue in scientific medical writing. This study aimed to examine the quotation error rate and trends over time in the medical literature. items.title: Proof Minimization in Neural Network Verification
items.abstract_600: The widespread adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs) requires efficient techniques for verifying their safety. DNN verifiers are complex tools, which might contain bugs that could compromise their soundness and undermine the reliability of the verification process. This concern can be mitigated using proofs: artifacts that are checkable by an external and reliable proof checker, and which attest to the correctness of the verification process. items.abstract_600: Deep research agents extend the role of search engines from retrieving keyword-matched pages to synthesizing knowledge, fundamentally changing how humans interact with information. items.title: EO-based long term cropland and paddy monitoring with the farm action toolkit (FAcT): strengthening policy support in Bhutan
items.abstract_600: Bhutan’s Five-Year Strategic Plan (FYP) guides national development, resource allocation, and food security. items.abstract_600: Current LLM-based research agents have advanced through agent orchestration, yet largely overlook scientific knowledge orchestration.
